to dims 0-2 of every step of the normalised chunk, only when the config has a nonzero servo_k (lifelong_ood/policy/backbone.py).  Every other config is bit-identical
(experiments/raas_b_test.py); for raas the served chunk equals PI0PytorchS.sample_actions on the same noise.  Hypothesis, contrasts, labels, states, bootstrap, margins and
analysis are SR 78's (experiments/prereg/raas_pred.txt, docs/notes/raas_plan.md), unchanged.  One unlabelled row is added: X7 = RAA-s (78b) - RAA-s (78, served without servo).

Predictions (probabilities are mine; they differ from SR 78's because the offline check says the expert plus servo sits at RAA-c's offline level, and RAA-c itself was .503).
1. S1 primary: SUPPORTED 7%, PARTIAL 8%, NOT SUPPORTED 85%.  Point estimate of S1a about -.07 (RAA-s 78b N1-N6 about .52, 80% range .38-.68).  Why near RAA-c: the offline
   chunk error equals RAA-c's (.176 vs .167) and the servo explains only about a third of the held-phase translation variance; the expert was trained on a residual and the
   release decision, not the commanded translation, may set where the object lands (SR 77).  Why not lower: the servo is exact in the channel and the training objective
   matched this serving.
2. S1a lower bound > 0 alone: 5%.  X3 > X2 (bottle gains more than cheese relative to RAA-o) in the point estimate: 50%.
3. S2 (RAA-s beats RAA, lower bound > 0): 4%.
4. S3: NON-INFERIOR to rgp (lower bound > -.10) 1%; beats rgp < 1%.
5. SK: RAA-s non-inferior to RAA-o on K1-K6 (lower bound > -.05): 12% (RAA-c was .814 against RAA-o .881).  K1-K6 success at least .80: 55%.  R0 fit gate (.85) holds: 99%.
6. Against RAA-c (X5 / X6, unlabelled): N1-N6 point estimate above RAA-c's .503: 50%; its 95% interval excludes 0 in either direction: 15%.  K1-K6 point above RAA-c's .814: 40%.
7. X7, 78b minus 78: positive on N1-N6 with lower bound > 0: 99% (the served path was broken by exactly the dropped term).
8. Plumbing: no routed query reached the model with an all-zero state in a held-target query, held-target channel median at test under 2 cm, and a bit-identical served chunk
   to PI0PytorchS.sample_actions on the same noise (shown offline before the rollouts): 90%.
9. Exploratory mechanism (labelled): median failed-release xy error on N4 at most 4.5 cm: 10%; on N1 and N4 both at most 2.5 cm: 2%; N4 and N6 not below RAA-o's (6.5 and 7.0 cm): 75%.
What would count against the claim: S1a lower bound <= 0 with N4 and N6 failed-release error not below RAA-o's.  What would count for it: S1a lower bound > 0 with N4 median failed-release
error below 5 cm.  A K1-K6 loss with an N1-N6 gain would be a trade, not a fix.  A result near RAA-c's (N1-N6 .50, K1-K6 .81) would say the state token, not the head, dominates.
